summary: The strict clipping inequality is proved correctly, including the equality and degenerate-boundary cases, but the stated nonexistence consequence is not established from the supplied candidate because the calibration terminology and its connection to the clipped areas are undefined.
critical_errors: The claimed consequence does not follow from the stated premises. The candidate never defines the "prescribed common-plane calibration" or states that c_i=|C_i|, c_l=|C_l|, and c_q=|C_q| for the three clips appearing in (1). Equation (12) only shows that the three numerical c-values sum to |K|; without the missing identification, (1) cannot be applied to those values, so nonexistence of A_0, A_2, K, the shifts, and the support data is unsupported.
gaps: Equation (2) invokes g_i, g_l, and g_q without defining them. The preceding direct halfplane-cover argument is sufficient, so this undefined assertion is unnecessary, but as written it is not verifiable.
repair_hints: State the exact common-plane calibration assumptions within the candidate, in particular the identities tying c_i, c_l, and c_q to the areas of the three explicitly defined clips of the same polygon K.
Remove equation (2), or define the g-quantities and prove the asserted pointwise identity.
